title: Neural networks give new warm-rain autoconversion and accretion parameterizations
summary: A deep feed-forward neural network trained on ARM Azores in situ cloud-probe data yielded parameterizations for autoconversion and accretion with about 15% and 5% uncertainty, outperforming existing ones. The analysis points to drizzle number concentration as a key factor for autoconversion, a variable missing from current parameterizations, and the authors say theory supports this. Testing used a held-out split from the same single campaign.
ai_technology: Deep feed-forward neural network (8 hidden layers, 1024 nodes) followed by symbolic optimization

evidence.tested: Held-out test split (about 4:1, 2.5 million points) from the ARM Azores field campaign.
evidence.unknown: Performance at other sites or campaigns.
evidence.ai_role: Predicts autoconversion and accretion rates and reveals the role of drizzle number concentration

source_review.scope: Abstract and Europe PMC full-text Methods/Results excerpts read. Publisher version not otherwise accessed. Author affiliations from OpenAlex metadata.
